Fractions and decimals

Numbers, sets, operations, proportional reasoning and numerical structure.

Maths / Number
FractionsEquivalent formsDecimalsNumber lineRich investigation

A fraction represents a number. We can place it on a number line, compare it with other fractions and express it as a decimal.

Interactive investigation: Farey Sequences

What happens when we list all the fractions between 0 and 1 in simplest form, allowing larger and larger denominators?

Open Farey Sequences ExplorerChange the denominator, see new fractions, order them on a number line and investigate patterns.

Start with F₃ or F₄. Predict first; use the app to check. There is no assessment gate.

1. Fractions on the number line

The fraction 3/4 lies three quarters of the way from 0 to 1. The fraction 1/2 lies at the midpoint.

To compare 2/5 with 1/2, use a common denominator: 2/5 = 4/10 and 1/2 = 5/10. Therefore 2/5 < 1/2.

2. Equivalent fractions and simplest form

2/4 = 1/2. They name the same number. We list 1/2 only once in a Farey sequence because every fraction is written in simplest form.

3. Connecting fractions and decimals

1/4 = 0.25, 1/2 = 0.5, 3/4 = 0.75. Some fractions give terminating decimals; others give recurring decimals. In the app, select a fraction to compare its exact and decimal forms.

4. Investigate before revealing

  1. Write F₃. Predict which fractions are added to make F₄.
  2. Explain why 2/6 is not a new entry when we move from F₅ to F₆.
  3. Investigate the lengths of F₁, F₂, F₃, … . Is every list longer than the previous one?
Discuss and check

F₄ adds 1/4 and 3/4. The fraction 2/6 reduces to 1/3, which is already present. Each list grows because 1/n is new at step n.

Further study: Sequences — the changing lengths of Farey sequences form another number sequence.
